newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO LEAVING BARCELONA, SAYS NUNEZ.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO LEAVING BARCELONA, SAYS NUNEZ.

text.p: Brazilian striker Ronaldo is to leave Barcelona, club president Jose Luiz Nunez said on Wednesday.
News of his impending departure came just one day after the Spanish club said the star striker had signed an improved nine-year contract.
"Ronaldo is leaving us," said Nunez who indicated the Brazilian striker could be headed for Italian club Inter Milan.
Nunez said he suspected after a negotiating session on Tuesday night that Ronaldo had already made a deal with Inter Milan.

"I believe that (Ronaldo's agents) were committed to Inter Milan because when they finished the meeting and shook our hands, afterward they spent almost one hour talking with the representatives of the Italian team," Nunez said.

Earlier on Wednesday, Spanish media reported that a dispute over a one-off 2.0 billion peseta ($14 million) bonus agreed last October had led to a suspension of the talks to keep the player at Barcelona.

The Spanish club reportedly said it would pay it to ensure Ronaldo did not go to another team. Barcelona wanted to pay the money through a company based in the Virgin Islands to save on taxes estimated at 1.0 billion pesetas ($7 million).
But Ronaldo's agents demanded the money be paid in Spain net of taxes. A spokesman for Barcelona said he had no comment on the reports.
The club said on Tuesday that Ronaldo had renewed his contract.

The 20-year-old striker signed on for nine more years at 500 million pesetas ($3.5 million) a season after protracted talks on the cost of breaking his contract, which was finally set at 10 billion pesetas ($69.9 million).
Italian, English and French clubs had shown interest in Ronaldo, whose 34 goals this season are far more than any other player in the Spanish league or the European Golden Boot competition.
